sources.title: GEMS Prize problem description (metric, submission format)
claims_verified: Metric is a distance-weighted Tversky index with alpha = 0.2 and beta = 0.8.
Triangular kernel k(d) = max(1 - d/R, 0) with R = 300 m (3 px at 100 m).
Submission is float32, single layer, values between 0 and 1, EPSG 32611, 100 m, same bounds as training data.
Data outside the bounds is null or nan.
sources.quote: Your submission contains a single layer with datatype of 32-bit float (`float32`) with values between 0 and 1 ... data outside the bounds is null or nan.
sources.irregularity: IRR-2026-10-27-02: the repo's promoted file zero-fills outside the footprint instead of NaN. The rule text allows null/nan outside bounds but does not forbid 0. Organizer confirmation is needed.

sources.title: GEMS Prize Official Rules (PDF, September 2026)
claims_verified: Three submissions per week (cited as 'three submissions per week' in Section 3.2 Process Overview).
Public-leaderboard scores may differ from final private-leaderboard scores.
First-round prize rankings use the selected final submissions against the private test set.
Competitors must choose a single submission for scoring across both rounds (stated on the OS-1 problem-description page, not in this PDF).
sources.quote: You can make multiple submissions, subject to the limits specified on the competition website (three submissions per week).

sources.title: DrivenData forum: known USGS/INGENIOUS fault pixels are masked when scoring
claims_verified: Staff (chrisk-dd, Sep 16) say pixels corresponding to known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are masked / excluded from evaluation, so they do not count toward penalty terms.
Staff say re-evaluation will also mask the existing USGS/INGENIOUS faults.
sources.quote: Pixels corresponding to known USGS/INGENIOUS faults are masked / excluded from evaluation, so they do not count towards penalty terms.

sources.title: DrivenData reference solution (GitHub)
claims_verified: Repository exists; contains unet-mc-cv-reference-solution.ipynb and no standalone scorer.
The notebook trains with segmentation_models_pytorch TverskyLoss(alpha=0.2, beta=0.8), which is a patch-level loss, not the distance-weighted DTI used for scoring.
sources.quote: from segmentation_models_pytorch.losses import TverskyLoss ... alpha = 0.2 ... beta = 0.8
sources.irregularity: IRR-2026-10-27-03: the official distance-weighted scorer is not public in this repo; the repo's DTI is a transcription of the OS-1 equations and is NOT an organizer-validated scorer.
